body.x: Futureduck Inc. (CEO Joy Kibbeum Na) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas, USA, at the K-Startup Pavilion.

Futureduck specializes in next-generation educational content and integrates advanced technology with education. The company emphasizes developing environments where learners benefit from AI's convenience without losing their creative edge. This approach ensures that AI technology complements rather than replaces the learning process.

Futureduck will introduce its writing education platform, Quewrite, at CES 2025. The platform leverages its proprietary “inquiring AI” model, Querius, designed to provide personalized writing guidance for each user. Quewrite’s core feature is its step-by-step writing instruction system. The AI model stimulates creativity by asking thought-provoking questions and offering feedback, encouraging learners to generate and articulate ideas effectively.

This approach enables students to foster independent thinking and develop writing skills, while educators can focus more on curriculum design rather than individual feedback. The platform alleviates the burden of manual corrections while enhancing the overall learning experience.

Currently, Quewrite is in beta testing and has garnered positive user feedback. It was previously showcased at the Edutech Korea Fair in September, where it impressed public and private education stakeholders with its ability to promote safe and effective AI usage while nurturing critical thinking skills. The platform has steadily gained traction in Korean classrooms, and Futureduck plans to leverage this success to expand into the North American and Southeast Asian edtech markets.

A Futureduck representative stated that the company aims to support children in the Fourth Industrial Revolution by helping them develop literacy and creativity skills to shape their futures. Presenting Quewrite at CES 2025 will highlight the platform’s vision of bridging the gap between technology and learning. The company also plans to gather feedback from diverse audiences, identify new market opportunities, and build partnerships with local stakeholders.

Futureduck focuses on markets with advanced edtech infrastructures, such as North America, and emerging markets like Singapore and Vietnam. By establishing a strong presence at CES 2025, the company hopes to secure a foundation for global expansion and further its mission as a leading edtech innovator.

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
